adjudication_label: Causal mechanisms of grain size evolution and refinement
canonical_question: What are the distinct mechanisms and boundary conditions governing grain size evolution, refinement, and anisotropy in refractory and equiatomic HEAs during annealing, severe plastic deformation, and additive manufacturing?

question_variants.question: Is the 'below 1 μm' grain size a result of pinning by the δ phase, and what evidence rules out Zener drag from other sources?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes the stabilization of grain size below 1 μm to a dispersion of the stable δ phase, consistent with Zener drag. However, it does not provide evidence explicitly ruling out Zener drag from other sources or other pinning mechanisms.

answers.answer: The grain size stabilized at below 1 μm due to a dispersion of the stable δ phase. No alternative sources for Zener drag are ruled out in the text.
answers.mechanism: Dispersion of stable δ phase (Zener drag implied).
answers.boundary_limitation: Other pinning sources not explicitly ruled out.
evidence_spans: Bulk (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (W30-Ni45-Fe20-Ta5, in at.%) alloy ingots were prepared by arc melting pure metals (all with purity >99.99%) in an argon atmosphere.
Alloy samples were repeatedly melted at least 10 times to ensure uniform melting and improve their chemical homogeneity.

After cooling, the bulk ingots with dimensions of 50 mm × 50 mm × 10 mm were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h in an Ar atmosphere and subsequently hot-rolled at 1200 °C with a rolling reduction ratio of 80%, i.e., with a thickness reduction from 10 to 2 mm.

source_evidence_spans: the grain size eventually stabilized at below 1 μm due to a dispersion of the stable δ phase

question_variants.question: Is the ~4 μm grain size in the MA-SPS-HPT specimen a result of dynamic recrystallization during HPT, or does it represent the original grain size preserved due to the cracking?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports a grain size of ~4 μm in the MA-SPS-HPT specimen and notes it was obtained from a piece of the specimen after it was damaged by cracking during the HPT process. It does not explicitly state whether this grain size is the result of dynamic recrystallization or the original preserved size.

answers.answer: The microstructure is described as having a 'grain size ~4 μm', but the text clarifies that 'the MA-SPS specimen was damaged during the HPT process, as many cracks emerged, and the specimen was separated into several smaller pieces' and 'The microstructure of this specimen shown in Figure 6 was obtained from one of these pieces.' The origin of this specific grain size (recrystallization vs preservation) is not explicitly resolved in the text.
answers.measurement_outcome: Grain size ~4 μm observed in a cracked fragment
answers.mechanism: Unclear if result of dynamic recrystallization or preserved
answers.boundary_limitation: Specimen broken during HPT; results from fragments only
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen consisted of an equiaxed very fine (grain size ~4 μm) microstructure with numerous precipitates and some amount of porosity (see Figure 6 ).
It should be accentuated that the MA-SPS specimen was damaged during the HPT process, as many cracks emerged, and the specimen was separated into several smaller pieces.
The microstructure of this specimen shown in Figure 6 was obtained from one of these pieces.

source_evidence_spans: The microstructure of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen consisted of an equiaxed very fine (grain size ~4 μm) microstructure with numerous precipitates and some amount of porosity (see Figure 6 ).

question_variants.question: Is the 'heat release to BD' in the TD/SD planes the only factor, or does the layer-by-layer cooling rate also contribute to the observed grain sizes?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes grain growth to heat release direction (epitaxial growth), specifically to the BD, but does not explicitly isolate or quantify the contribution of layer-by-layer cooling rates versus heat release direction in the TD/SD planes.

answers.answer: The text states that grains grow in the direction of heat release during AM, considering epitaxial growth as heat is released to the BD. It does not explicitly state if layer-by-layer cooling rate is a separate contributing factor in TD/SD planes or if it is subsumed under the heat release concept.
answers.measurement_outcome: Epitaxial growth observed along heat release direction (BD).
answers.mechanism: Grain growth directed by heat release; epitaxial growth considered as heat released to BD.
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific contribution of cooling rate separate from heat release direction is not detailed.
evidence_spans: Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.
The pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi powder had a spherical shape, and was confirmed to have an even distribution of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni elements.
The average diameter of the initial powders was measured as 27.2 um ( d 10 = 17.9 µm, d 50 = 26.1 µm, d 90 = 38.2 µm).

source_evidence_spans: the grains grow in the direction of heat release during AM, and thus it is considered that epitaxial growth appears as heat is released to BD

question_variants.question: Is the 378 nm ultra-fine grain size consistent with the 'slip and partial RX' mechanism, or does it suggest a different threshold?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence confirms the existence of 378 nm grains and mentions a 'slip and partial RX' context but does not explicitly link the 378 nm size to this specific mechanism or define a threshold value for it.

answers.answer: The text states that 'ultra-fine grains with an average size of 378 nm were found at grain boundaries,' but does not specify if this is consistent with a 'slip and partial RX' threshold or suggest a different one.
answers.boundary_limitation: No threshold value for slip and partial RX is provided in the evidence.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: Grain size in HEAs is determined by a competition between driving forces (stored energy from deformation, thermal activation) and pinning/resistance mechanisms (Zener drag, epitaxial growth directionality). However, the specific mechanism yielding a stable grain size or a specific morphology is highly dependent on the processing route (annealing, HPT, SLM) and the microstructural constituents present (secondary phases, cracks).
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: Papers approach this by isolating specific processing regimes: one focuses on thermal stabilization via secondary phase dispersion (PMC10213035), another on the ambiguous outcome of mechanical deformation on damaged specimens (PMC6926650), a third on the scale of deformation-induced structures (PMC7229066), and a final one on the directional kinetics of additive manufacturing (PMC7229066).
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The dominant mechanism shifts from Zener drag by δ-phase at 900 °C (PMC10213035) to potential dynamic recrystallization (or preservation) at room temperature HPT (PMC6926650) to slip/partial recrystallization at specific boundary regions (PMC7229066). Additionally, in AM, the heat release direction (BD) dictates growth over the cooling rate magnitude (PMC7229066).
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions exist between the papers; rather, they report distinct observations under incompatible or undefined conditions. For instance, a stable <1 μm size is attributed to pinning (PMC10213035), while a ~4 μm size in a cracked specimen has an unresolved origin regarding recrystallization vs. preservation (PMC6926650), and 378 nm grains are observed without a defined threshold for the mechanism (PMC7229066).
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Evidence for the δ-phase pinning mechanism is strong for the specific W-Ni-Fe-Ta alloy at 900 °C (PMC10213035), but evidence for the origin of the ~4 μm grains in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy is weak due to specimen damage (PMC6926650). The link between 378 nm grains and specific RX thresholds is observational but lacks quantitative threshold definition (PMC7229066).
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: It is unresolved whether the ~4 μm grain size in the HPT specimen represents a recrystallized state or a preserved state due to the specimen cracking (PMC6926650), and whether the 378 nm ultra-fine grains observed at boundaries represent a known threshold for slip and partial RX or a distinct regime (PMC7229066). Furthermore, the contribution of layer-by-layer cooling rates to grain orientation in AM, distinct from the heat release direction, remains undefined (PMC7229066).
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: Grain size stability in HEAs is not governed by a single universal threshold but by a regime-specific balance where Zener drag dominates in annealed two-phase systems, while deformation-induced recrystallization thresholds are obscured by mechanical instability (cracking) or are undefined in the absence of explicit kinetic data.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Conduct room-temperature HPT on the HfNbTaTiZr alloy without inducing cracks, followed by post-mortem TEM to distinguish between preserved grain boundaries and new low-angle/high-angle boundaries indicative of dynamic recrystallization. Simultaneously, vary the cooling rate in SLM while maintaining constant heat release direction to isolate the contribution of cooling rate vs. directionality on TD/SD plane grain growth.
